page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-intel is an entry-level virtual private server belonging to the High Performance family. It features an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor configured with 2 vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled to provide 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and utilizes a shared CPU allocation model. Memory capacity is set at 4.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 100 GB of NVMe SSD space, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations place this server in the lower tiers of performance. The stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1391.28 and multi-core score of 2729.87 are categorized in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is constrained, with large-block read bandwidth at 11.67 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 9.16 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 982.0 and a multi-core score of 1733.0. Database operations, such as Redis SET performance at 2.57 million operations per second, and LLM inference tasks also rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting the limitations of the shared CPU architecture.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require dedicated CPU resources. The inclusion of 100 GB of NVMe SSD storage provides a solid storage-to-compute ratio for budget-conscious deployments. However, the shared CPU allocation and weak memory bandwidth present clear performance tradeoffs under sustained loads. This instance is best suited for lightweight workloads such as static web serving, basic application testing, small utility scripts, and low-traffic development environments.
